The initial wet weight at birth is correspondingly minuscule, calculated at 0.00000723 grams [Wwb = 0.00000723 grams] based on the spherical egg diameter, a mass that underscores the extreme economy of maternal investment in this gelatinous zooplankter. Field studies suggest that individuals attain a maximum trunk length of 0.15 cm [Li = 0.15 cm] upon completing somatic growth, which represents roughly a six-fold increase from the neonatal size. This modest asymptotic dimension is typical of the Fritillariidae, which generally achieve smaller body sizes compared to their oikopleurid relatives, a divergence often attributed to differences in filtering apparatus architecture and the associated hydrodynamic constraints on particle capture.

The onset of reproductive competence in this species is tightly linked to the birth event itself, as the trunk length at puberty is identical to the length at birth at 0.024 cm [Lp = 0.024 cm], a pattern also observed in the related species Oikopleura dioica. This coincidence implies that individuals are capable of gamete production immediately upon hatching, an extreme life-history strategy that maximises the probability of reproducing within a very short lifespan. Throughout the brief juvenile interval, which may be functionally absent given the immediate reproductive capacity, the organism must simultaneously grow and invest in gonadal development, a trade-off that likely constrains the ultimate body size attainable before senescence.

Over the course of its abbreviated existence, the organism accumulates substantial somatic mass, culminating in a dry weight at death of 0.00000912 grams , representing more than a 280-fold increase from the neonatal dry mass. Temperature is a critical determinant of developmental rate in appendicularians, and populations inhabiting colder waters may exhibit extended generation times, although quantitative data for Fritillaria pellucida across a thermal gradient remain scarce.

Comparative studies with other appendicularians reveal that the life-history strategy of Fritillaria pellucida is characterised by an extreme compression of the reproductive phase. In many oikopleurids, a distinct juvenile growth period precedes the onset of gametogenesis, yet in this species that period is functionally eliminated because puberty and birth coincide.
